{{Short description|British mathematician (1950–2019)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2025}}
{{Use British English|date=July 2025}}

'''Stephen Theodore Chesmer Siklos''' (27 March 1950 – 17 August 2019) was a British mathematician, astrophysicist and university administrator. For his doctorate, he undertook research into [[general relativity]] under [[Stephen Hawking]]. After completing two postdoctoral positions, he spent the remainder of his career at the [[University of Cambridge]]. He was at various times a lecturer in the Faculty of Mathematics, Director of Studies for Mathematics at [[Newnham College, Cambridge|Newnham College]] and [[Jesus College, Cambridge|Jesus College]] and Senior Tutor at Jesus College. He is best known for his work in setting up and administering the [[Sixth Term Examination Papers]], used for undergraduate mathematics admissions at several British universities.<ref name=Guardian>{{cite web |last1=Clackson |first1=James |author-link1=James Clackson|title=Stephen Siklos obituary |url=https://www.theguardian.com/education/2019/sep/23/stephen-siklos-obituary |website=The Guardian |language=en |date=23 September 2019}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Siklos was born in [[Epsom]], Surrey, England in 1950, the son of Theodore Siklos, the first principal of [[Crawley College|Crawley College of Further Education]], and Ruth Siklos (née Purser), an almoner.<ref name=Guardian/> He was educated at [[The College of Richard Collyer|Collyer's School]] in [[Horsham]] before reading for the [[Mathematical Tripos]] at [[Pembroke College, Cambridge|Pembroke College]], Cambridge, where he obtained a distinction in Part III and was also awarded the [[Tyson Medal]]. He then spent a year teaching at [[Dulwich College]], London.<ref name="uc">{{cite web |title=Stephen Siklos, 1950-2019 |url=https://www.maths.cam.ac.uk/features/stephen-siklos-1950-2019 |publisher=University of  Cambridge |access-date=24 June 2025}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
In 1973, he began a PhD into [[general relativity]], supervised by [[Stephen Hawking]]. In 1976, his dissertation, entitled "Singularities, Invariants and Cosmology",<ref>{{cite web |title=Stephen Siklos - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=115560 |website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref> led to a long-term interest in schemes for assessing the relative generality of solutions of [[Einstein field equations|Einstein's equations]] and to the study of what are now known as'' Siklos invariants'', ''Siklos universes'' and ''Siklos waves''.<ref name="uc"/>

Following his dissertation, his two PhD examiners hired him successively for postdoctoral posts, first [[Dennis W. Sciama|Dennis Sciama]] at the Department of Astrophysics at [[Oxford University|Oxford]], and then from 1978 Malcolm MacCallum at Queen Mary College (now [[Queen Mary University of London]]).<ref name=Guardian/><ref name="uc"/>

Following these posts, he spent the rest of his career at [[Cambridge University|Cambridge]]. From 1980 to 1999 he was a lecturer and later Director of Studies in Mathematics at [[Newnham College, Cambridge|Newnham College]], and from 1991 held a part-time university lectureship  in the [[Faculty of Mathematics, University of Cambridge|Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics]] (DAMTP). In 1999, he became a fellow of  [[Jesus College, Cambridge|Jesus College]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/reporter/2008-09/special/03/14.html |website=Cambridge University Reporter |publisher=Cambridge University Press |access-date=21 July 2025|title=Fellows of the Colleges: Jesus College|year=2008}}</ref> In the same year  he was awarded the Pilkington Teaching Prize for the "outstanding quality" of his teaching. He served as the college's Director of Studies in Mathematics, and later as its Senior Tutor.<ref name="uc"/><ref name="new">{{cite web |last1=Barlow |first1=Claire |title=A tribute to Stephen Siklos (1950-2019) |url=https://newn.cam.ac.uk/newnham-news/tribute-stephen-siklos-1950-2019 |website=Newnham College |access-date=24 June 2025 |language=en |date=24 September 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Pilkington Prize Winners |url=https://www.cctl.cam.ac.uk/files/all_prize_winners.pdf |website=University of Cambridge |access-date=25 June 2025 |page=27}}</ref> In 2017 and 2018 he was its President, the highest college office below that of Master.

During his time at DAMTP, he served as Chair of the Teaching Committee, Faculty Admissions Officer and Mathematics Subject Convenor for the Admissions Forum. He is credited with successfully guiding the faculty through the national Teaching Assessment Exercise and the subsequent changes to the undergraduate [[Tripos]].<ref name="uc" />

=== STEP ===
In 1987, Siklos played a central role in setting up the [[Sixth Term Examination Papers]] (STEP), a series of examinations taken by candidates for admission to mathematics courses at Cambridge and other universities regardless of their previous mathematical training.<ref name="step">{{cite web |title=Sixth Term Examination Papers (STEP) |url=https://www.maths.cam.ac.uk/undergrad/admissions/step |website=Undergraduate Admissions |publisher=University of Cambridge |access-date=26 June 2025 |language=en}}</ref> He led the project for 32 years during which he steered STEP through major changes in schools' mathematics curricula. He was involved in  every stage of the examination process, including drafting questions, scrutinising the final papers and directing the marking and grading. Seen as "the public face of STEP", he gave talks about the project at faculty open days, led the faculty's long-running STEP Easter School and established its STEP support programme.<ref name="uc" /> Writing in ''[[The Guardian]]'', [[James Clackson]] said that Siklos "did more than anyone to make the Cambridge entrance examination in mathematics accessible to students whatever their school background".<ref name=Guardian/>

== Publications ==
* {{cite book |editor1-last=Gibbons |editor1-first=G.W. |editor2-last=Hawking |editor2-first=S.W. |editor3-last= Siklos |editor3-first=S.T.C. |title=The very early Universe |date=1983 |publisher= Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0521316774 |edition=reprint}} The proceedings of the Nuffield Workshop on the Very Early Universe which took place in DAMTP in the summer of 1982.<ref name="cosmo">{{cite web |title=Stephen Siklos, 1950-2019 |url=https://www.ctc.cam.ac.uk/news/190605_newsitem.php |website=Centre for Theoretical Cosmology |publisher=University of Cambridge}}</ref>

* {{cite book |last1=Siklos |first1=S |title=Philippa Fawcett and the Mathematical Tripos |date=1990 |publisher=Newnham College |location=Cambridge}} Written to mark the centenary of [[Philippa Fawcett]] becoming the first woman to obtain the top score in the Cambridge Mathematical Tripos.

* {{cite book |last1=Siklos |first1=Stephen |title=Advanced Problems in Mathematics: Preparing for University |date=2019 |publisher=[[Open Book Publishers]] |isbn=978-1-78374-776-4 |edition=2nd}} A guide for STEP candidates, aimed at equipping students to take STEP even if their school could not provide the necessary support or guidance. The book contains selected past questions, with each question being accompanied by a comment and a full solution. This 2019 edition is a revised and extended version of two earlier editions by Siklos. It is available in [[PDF]] format to STEP candidates free of charge.<ref name = "step" /><ref name="cosmo" />

== Personal life and death ==
His extracurricular interests included music (he played the violin and viola), bridge and tennis.<ref name=Guardian/> 

Stephen Siklos died from cancer in 2019. He was survived by his wife, [[Marian Holness|Professor Marian Holness]], their two sons Arthur and Edward, by the children from his first marriage to Catherine (née Marshall), Tabitha and Jonathan, and his brother Paul.<ref name="uc"/>
